calls.reason: Neither Nestler's posted o3 proof nor any independent check of it was recovered, so only Marcus's own assertion says it was invalid.
The original USAMO evaluation (Petrov et al.) says all evaluated LLMs consistently claimed to have solved the problems, which matches Marcus's description.

The Nature Machine Intelligence study found users overestimate LLM accuracy and that longer explanations raise confidence. Microsoft Research saw that AI interfaces don't encourage checking and that users resisted being told sources were fake.
The claim rests on what the authors had personally seen. Earlier studies are mixed (one found prompting improved abstention, another little benefit) and neither covers proofs.
AlphaProof's Lean kernel check supports immunity, but a later paper found a wrong step in an original AlphaGeometry proof. Nothing shows AlphaGeometry 2 is guaranteed sound, so the evidence is mixed.

The Tow Center study found high error rates on one narrow citation task, and the YouGov survey shows trust split rather than a broad expectation of reliability. Neither study measures non-specialist users specifically.
